question: Spain’s Civil Guard has arrested a former senior official from the Ministry for Ecological Transition for alleged involvement in a corruption scheme concerning the authorisation of wind- and solar-energy projects.

The accused, who served as deputy director during Commissioner Teresa Ribera’s tenure as minister, is being investigated for environmental crime, bribery, money laundering and membership of a criminal organisation. According to reports, he demanded that all environmental assessments relating to Forestalia projects be submitted to him in order to expedite their approval.
After his retirement, moreover, he was hired as a consultant to this same ministry.

Given that some of these energy projects may have received EU funding and the fact that Forestalia received subsidies managed by Spain’s Directorate-General for EU Funds: Does the Commission intend to ask Commissioner Teresa Ribera for clarification on her management during that period and on the safeguards put in place to ensure full compliance with EU law and protect its financial interests?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2026) The information and allegations set out by the Honourable Members in their question relate to matters which, according to the question, are being investigated by the Spanish competent authorities. For any matters falling within the Commission’s competence, it stands ready to cooperate with national authorities where necessary and relevant. At this stage, the Commission has not been contacted by the Spanish authorities in the matter.
